reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about defect formation, thermal gradients, and the effects of pre-heating in CoCrFeMnNi LPBF, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific alloy–process–temperature combination proposed.
premises: Room-temperature LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi produces high thermal gradients, residual stresses, porosity, and delamination
Pre-heating substrate to ~500°C reduces thermal gradients during LPBF
Reduced thermal gradients lead to fewer solidification defects and lower residual stresses
Fewer defects and lower stresses improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity
The effect is specific to CoCrFeMnNi LPBF under argon at ~500°C pre-heat
